_doc: Squad topology as an executable artifact (FOC-158). Until now the graph lived in prose (agents/*/CLAUDE.md) plus four routing rules in config/handoff-rules.json — it could not be drawn, diffed or validated. This file is the source of truth for BOTH: node contracts (what each squad consumes, produces, when it is done, what it emits on failure) and the typed edges between them. Validate + render: node scripts/graph-validate.mjs [--emit-puml|--emit-handoff-rules]. Full rationale: docs/plans/brainstorm-graph-engineering.md
_migration: config/handoff-rules.json is currently the file telemetry-server.mjs reads at runtime. It is being retired: this graph is authoritative, and `--emit-handoff-rules` regenerates that file from these edges. The regeneration is not a permanent view — it is the EQUIVALENCE PROOF for the migration. graph-validate.test.mjs asserts the committed handoff-rules.json is exactly what these edges produce, which is the mechanical evidence that nothing was lost in translation. When telemetry-server.mjs is rewired to read this file directly, handoff-rules.json, the emitter and that drift test are deleted together.
_entryNodes: Nodes legitimately reachable without an inbound edge. `plan` is triggered by an entry in planning/inbox/ (a voice memo, an artefact) before any Linear task exists; `cadence` is triggered by a weekly timer, not by a task at all. Every other node MUST have an inbound edge — a node nothing routes to is dead topology, and graph-validate.mjs fails on it.
_autonomy: Per-node autonomy level, human-set ONLY. Every node ships as `supervised`; promotion to `bounded` or `scheduled` is a committed edit by Mateusz backed by telemetry evidence, never something the system grants itself (brainstorm A decision #1 stays literal). Hard precondition: no node may go below `supervised` before FOC-163 (grounded verdicts) exists — promoting a node whose evaluator judges by eye is how parallelism turns into scaled-up unverified work.
_budget: Stage each node's spend belongs to, for the per-stage allocation in FOC-162 (B_discovery + B_verification + B_synthesis + B_reserve). shareHint is a starting split of an issue budget, to be tuned from usage_facts once real runs exist — it is a hint, not a measured value. The reserve is held at graph level because it belongs to no single node.
_concurrency: Maximum simultaneous live children per node. All 1 today, which is the WIP=1 the squads already enforce by hand. FOC-161 (semaphore + backpressure) reads these instead of hardcoding a limit.

budgetPolicy.note: Released last, covers retries and tool failures only. Exhaustion stops graph expansion and produces a partial-status report (FOC-162).

input.description: An entry in the planning inbox — voice memo, artefact, free-text idea. No Linear task exists yet, or a Draft does.

plan.completion: Idempotent push to Linear succeeded AND the hand-off comment is posted. Re-running must not duplicate issues.
plan.failure: A HITL gate did not get its ✅ → stop without pushing. NEVER push to Linear without GATE 2 approval.

input.description: Exactly one issue, dependency-aware: anything with unfinished blockers is skipped. Prefer the smallest estimate.

output.git: branch off main, commits on that branch — never pushed

linear.comment: hand-off summary (what changed, self-verification, open questions)

dev.completion: Work is committed on the squad branch AND the hand-off comment is posted AND the issue is transitioned to In Review — REVIEW needs a real diff to read.
dev.failure: Two failed attempts → labels `escalated` + `needs:answer`, write .state/dev-wip.json, exit cleanly. Never busy-wait.

input.description: Reads the branch diff. Three passes run concurrently: first-pass, security, deep.

pass.state: In Review (unchanged — hands to TEST without a transition)

review.completion: A verdict is posted. Clean = every AC and DoD item passes with zero blocking `issue:` findings.
review.failure: round > 2 (third attempt) → label `escalated`, post the final verdict, STOP and notify Mateusz. Max 2 dev↔review cycles.

input.description: Picked up after REVIEW approved and assigned a version.

test.completion: Deploy health-check passed AND synthetic tests passed. The health-check is mandatory before E2E and carries auto-rollback.
test.failure: Loop-limit reached → escalate. A failed health-check rolls back before anything else runs.

input.description: Time-triggered, not task-triggered — this is why cadence is an entry node. Reads workspace state; does not pick an issue.

linear.comment: digest posted to the active epic

cadence.failure: Collector cannot reach Linear → report the gap in the digest rather than inventing numbers.

input.description: Any task waiting on Mateusz: needs:answer, needs:approval, needs:decision, needs:access.

output.description: An answer, approval or decision that removes the needs:* label and unblocks the task.

human.failure: None — this node does not fail, it waits. Nothing may route past it while the label is set.

edges.why: needs:* → human (HOW-TO §6: any needs:answer/approval/decision/access = waiting on Mateusz, stop). Evaluated first so a blocked task always routes to the human regardless of state. Wildcard is separator-agnostic in the matcher — matches both the colon form (needs:answer, HOW-TO §6 doc convention) and the hyphen form (needs-decision, the actual Linear label name in this workspace).
In Review + coded → review (DEV→REVIEW handoff). Linear exposes the leaf label `coded` (linear-ops.mjs accepts `ai:coded` as an add-alias, but the API returns `coded`).
stage:testing → test (REVIEW→TEST handoff, after approve + version).

REVIEW sends work back by transitioning to In Progress. This matches NO rule in handoff-rules.json today (the DEV rule requires Todo), so returns route to null in the dashboard — a real gap, made visible here rather than left implicit. NOT routable yet, for two reasons. (1) Emitting it would break the equivalence proof against the committed handoff-rules.json. (2) The blocking one: `In Progress` is ALSO the state of a task DEV is actively working on, so routing it to dev would suggest dev for work dev already holds. Enabling this needs a discriminator for 'returned, round > 0' — a round label or a state — which does not exist yet. That is a separate task with a visible dashboard behaviour change, not a side effect of declaring the topology.

TEST sends a failed deploy or failed synthetic back to DEV as In Progress, with a root-cause report. Same discriminator problem as review-to-dev-return, and indistinguishable from it by state+labels alone — another reason the round marker is a prerequisite.

Two failed attempts in DEV. Not routable because the `escalated` label is always set together with `needs:answer`, so the order-1 gate edge already routes these to the human — a routable rule here would be dead code that never wins first-match.

round > 2, i.e. a third dev↔review attempt. Declared so the escalation path is visible in the topology; routing is handled by the order-1 gate edge. FOC-163 replaces the round counter with a diff+failure fingerprint, which will change this edge's condition.
TEST loop-limit reached. Same routing note as the other escalate edges.

PLAN's two HITL gates. Not routable: today they block inline in the PLAN REPL and are never expressed as Linear state, so there is nothing for a label matcher to see. FOC-122 turns them into gate records relayed by the Supervisor, at which point this edge gains an observable condition.
